Chernobyl: 85±26 PBq; Fukushima: 13.6 PBq atmospheric; ~3.5 PBq directly to ocean

notes: Chernobyl: 2 immediate deaths + 28 ARS; Fukushima: 0 radiation deaths; 1 worker cardiac arrest on cleanup (not radiation)
Key difference: RBMK graphite fire burned openly for 10 days at high temperature driving radionuclides to high altitude; BWR reactor vessel contained meltdown
Chernobyl max confirmed ARS dose ~16 Gy; Fukushima max confirmed worker dose 180 mGy (non-lethal); vast difference in worker protection
Iodine-131 equivalent accounting for Cs-137 longevity (multiply Cs-137 by 40): Chernobyl ~5200 PBq-Ie; Fukushima ~770 PBq-Ie; ~6.7x ratio
External Cs-137 doses to humans from soil: PMC7220933 comparative study confirms Chernobyl exposure significantly higher in most metrics
RBMK positive void coefficient (steam bubbles increase reactivity) was root cause of Chernobyl runaway; modern BWR/PWR have negative void coefficients; RBMK design no longer built
Chernobyl reactor building had no Western-style primary containment; explosion destroyed building completely; Fukushima had containment that was damaged but held most inventory
